sentences.text: The Disability Royal Commission was asked how governments, institutions and the community could prevent violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation and support greater inclusion of people with disability.
sentences.support:
Our terms of reference require us to inquire into what governments, institutions 
and the community should do

sentences.text: Its inquiry considered experiences across different settings and stages of life, using hearings, community engagement, submissions, private sessions and research.
sentences.support:
we gathered information through public hearings, 
community engagements, submissions, responses to issues papers, private sessions, policy 
work, research and data analysis.

sentences.text: The Commission found that people with disability continued to face high levels of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation, alongside exclusion from many areas of life.
sentences.support:
Our inquiry has shown people with disability continue to experience high rates of violence 
and abuse, multiple forms of neglect, and sexual and financial exploitation.

sentences.text: Its 222 recommendations seek to prevent harm, protect human rights and improve inclusion, with coordinated implementation and independent monitoring.
sentences.section: Scope of the inquiry; Beyond the Royal Commission
sentences.support: The Final report contains a total of 222 recommendations.

findings.quote:
Our inquiry has shown people with disability continue to experience high rates of violence 
and abuse, multiple forms of neglect, and sexual and financial exploitation.

Based on their disability, people with disability continue to be 
excluded from participating in many areas of life.

notes: The executive summary includes endnotes through PDF page 212; its narrative ends on PDF page 207. Some recommendations reflect differing Commissioner positions, so the summary does not imply unanimity on individual models of service provision.
